leads.name: yosymfony/toml
leads.note: TOML 0.4.0; likely rejects hexadecimal integers and dotted keys.
leads.evidence: Toml::parse(file_get_contents('controls/toml/typed-scalars.toml')) throws Yosymfony\Toml\Exception\ParseException: Syntax error: unexpected token "T_UNQUOTED_KEY" at line 6 with value "xDEAD_BEEF". Expected T_NEWLINE or T_EOS. (hex = 0xDEAD_BEEF; the release implements TOML 0.4.0, which has no hexadecimal, octal or binary integers). Loading the release on PHP 8.5 also raises E_DEPRECATED implicit-nullable notices.
leads.checked_with: PHP 8.5.12 CLI, composer install of the pinned release

leads.name: devium/toml
leads.evidence: service-config.toml matches its typed tree exactly. typed-scalars.toml differs only at times.local_time: 00:32:00.25 is returned as Devium\Toml\TomlLocalTime {hour: 0, minute: 32, second: 0, millisecond: 25}; TomlLocalTime::fromString() takes intval() of the fraction digits, so .25 s becomes 25 ms (the README documents millisecond 999 for .999999), giving 00:32:00.025 instead of 00:32:00.25. Its __toString() prints .25 only because it echoes the same integer. Without asFloat the decoder returns fractional floats such as 3.25 as strings (documented default).
leads.checked_with: PHP 8.5.12 CLI, composer install of the pinned release

leads.name: jamesmoss/toml
leads.checked_with: composer:2 image (PHP 8.5.12 CLI), composer require of the release
leads.evidence: Toml\Parser::fromString rejects service-config.toml with 'Unknown primative for `{ max = 10, min = -2 }` on line 14' (no inline tables) and typed-scalars.toml with 'Unknown primative for `+99` on line 4'; the 2014 parser predates TOML 0.4.

leads.name: leonelquinteros/php-toml
leads.checked_with: composer:2 image (PHP 8.5.12 CLI), composer require of the release
leads.evidence: Toml::parse returns service-config inline tables as stdClass objects mixed with arrays, and rejects typed-scalars.toml with 'Unknown value type: 0xDEAD_BEEF' (no hexadecimal integers).

leads.name: zidizei/toml-php
leads.checked_with: composer:2 image (PHP 8.5.12 CLI), composer require of the release
leads.evidence: Toml\Toml::parse rejects service-config.toml with "Unrecognized data type '{' on line 13 near column 10" (no inline tables) and typed-scalars.toml with "Unrecognized data type '+99' on line 3 near column 14".

leads.name: app-hive/toml
leads.checked_with: php:8.5-cli image (sha256:50956f094e90a716d43bea28087d447555ad80510e386ab8c9c10d8c70d781a9) with gmp and bcmath added, composer install of the release
leads.evidence: Toml::parse needs ext-gmp, which composer.json does not declare (without it typed-scalars fails with 'Call to undefined function AppHive\Toml\Parser\gmp_strval()'). With gmp, integers, floats and strings of both controls are correct, but every date-time comes back as a plain string ('1979-05-27T00:32:00.5-07:00', '1979-05-27T07:32:00', '1979-05-27', '00:32:00.25'), indistinguishable from a TOML string; ParserConfig only toggles strictness, and Parser::parse() returns the same array, so no documented API keeps the four date-time kinds.

leads.name: petalbranch/toml
leads.checked_with: composer:2 image (PHP 8.5.12 CLI), composer require of the release
leads.evidence: Toml::parse returns correct integers, floats, strings and keys for typed-scalars, but formats all four date-time kinds back to plain strings, so the array API fails the typed tree. Its Parser::parseToNode returns a node tree whose ValueNode::getType() carries TomlType (OFFSET_DATETIME, LOCAL_DATETIME, LOCAL_DATE, LOCAL_TIME); a harness over that node tree (the round-1 php-collective/toml approach) was not built in this round.

leads.name: dayvsonspacca/psl-toml
leads.checked_with: php:8.5-cli image (sha256:50956f094e90a716d43bea28087d447555ad80510e386ab8c9c10d8c70d781a9) with gmp and bcmath added, composer install of the release
leads.evidence: Toml::parse needs ext-bcmath (undeclared). With it, service-config parses, but typed-scalars gives floats.negative = integer 0 for -0.5, keeps the line-ending backslash of the multi-line basic string ('first \\\n  second'), and returns the local date as a DateTimeImmutable carrying the current time of day and the local time on the current date, so local kinds are not represented.
